chunks: Al-Ḥalabī asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about killing snakes, and he said:
"Kill everything you find in the wilderness except the jān."

And he forbade killing the dwellers of houses and said: "Do not leave them out of fear of their consequences, for the Jews in the time of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to say: whoever killed a house-dweller would be afflicted by such-and-such. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: whoever leaves them out of fear of their consequences is not from me; rather, you leave it because it does not intend you."
And he said: "Sometimes I killed them in their houses."

key_terms.الْجَانَّ: the jān; here an excluded category mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.عَوَامِرِ الْبُيُوتِ: house-dwelling creatures or beings referred to as the inhabitants of homes
key_terms.مَخَافَةَ تَبِعَاتِهِنَّ: out of fear of their consequences or repercussions

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about killing snakes and the ʿawāmir of houses?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling on killing snakes and distinguishes between what is found in the wilderness and the house-dwelling creatures referred to as ʿawāmir al-buyūt. It also rejects superstitious fear of supposed consequences from killing them, grounding conduct instead in the guidance of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4234 - Al-Halabi asked Abu Abdullah (as) about killing snakes.
Imam (as) said: "Kill everything you find in the wilderness except the jinn."

And he forbade killing the household spirits (ʿAwamir) and said:
"Do not leave them out of fear of their consequences, for the Jews during the time of the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, used to say that whoever killed a household spirit would suffer such-and-such misfortune."
Then the Messenger of Allah (swt), peace be upon him and his family, said:
"Whoever refrains from killing them out of fear of their consequences is not from me. Rather, leave them alone because they do not intend to harm you."
Imam (as) also said: "I sometimes killed them in their houses."
